title: api-gateway: adjust streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and payload limits for OpenAI-compat tool calls
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: customers running streaming tool/function-calling workloads under the OpenAI compatibility layer observed intermittent stalls and increased memory usage when large payloads or many concurrent streaming sessions hit the API gateway. The proxy's default internal buffer growth and some routing decisions caused backpressure to be applied unevenly across routes, which surfaced as slow or dropped streaming chunks and occasional tool-call timeouts. This change introduces conservative per-route streaming buffer caps, a new routing preference for low-latency streaming hosts, and payload size guardrails for OpenAI-compat endpoints that perform function/tool calls. The PR also preserves chunked transfer semantics across the proxy and adds metadata headers used by the OpenAI-compat adapter to correctly reassemble function call events. Checklist: - Add per-route streaming buffer cap and overall proxy memory ceiling - Adjust routing policy to prefer streaming-optimized backends when request indicates chunked streaming or tool-calls - Enforce configurable payload size limits for OpenAI-compat tool-call requests and surface 413 with clear diagnostics - Preserve Transfer-Encoding: chunked and include redwood-stream-id header to improve tracing across retries - Add unit + integration tests that simulate high-concurrency streaming tool-calls and large payloads - Update docs and release notes for API surface behavior changes Link to related incident: SUP-4421. Linear: ENG-1876. This is intended as a non-breaking behavioral change but may require customers that rely on implicit large-payload passthrough to review limits. Default limits are conservative and configurable via gateway config.

release_notes:
- API Gateway: introduce per-route streaming buffer caps and proxy-wide memory ceiling to improve streaming stability under high concurrency.
- Routing: prefer streaming-optimized backends for chunked Transfer-Encoding and long-running tool/function-call sessions.
- OpenAI-compat: enforce configurable payload size limits for function/tool-call endpoints; return structured 413 errors when exceeded.
- Transfer-Encoding: chunked preserved end-to-end and redwood-stream-id header added for tracing across retries.
notes_for_ops: Default streaming buffer cap is 8MB per route and 1GB proxy-wide. These defaults can be adjusted via api-gateway config. Monitor gateway.memory.peak and streaming.reassembly.errors after rollout. If customers need higher passthrough limits, escalate with SUP ticket and config override.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for buffer cap enforcement and router preference heuristics. Integration test simulates 500 concurrent streaming tool-calls with 2MB payloads each, validating no stalls and correct reassembly of function call events. CI initially failed due to a test harness race; fixed by adding a short jitter in test setup and rerun.
impact: Small behavioral change to API surface: requests exceeding new limits will receive structured 413 errors. Streaming behavior should be more stable and low-latency for tool-call workloads due to routing preferences.
